headline: Teaching is the art of causing understanding—and it deepens the teacher's understanding too
universal_truth: To teach is to learn twice; explaining to others reveals gaps in your own understanding
fun_facts: Students who teach material to others retain 90% compared to 10% for reading alone
The 'Feynman Technique' for learning: explain it like you're teaching a child, find gaps, simplify, repeat
Children who tutor younger children improve their own performance significantly
discussion_questions: What have you learned better by teaching?
Who taught you something that stuck?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Want to really learn something? Teach it. The moment you try to explain, you discover what you don't actually understand. Teaching isn't just sharing knowledge—it's a powerful method for creating knowledge, for both teacher and student.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Anyone can talk about a topic. But causing genuine understanding in another person is an art. What makes teaching actually work?

options.text: Effective teaching starts from where the learner is, builds on what they already know, uses multiple approaches, and checks for understanding
options.response: Yes. Teaching isn't about displaying knowledge—it's about bridging from what someone knows to what they don't. The learner's state, not the teacher's knowledge, is the starting point.

options.text: Knowing the subject deeply makes you a good teacher
options.response: Expertise helps, but many experts can't teach—understanding transmission requires different skills...

q1.title: To Teach Is to Learn
q1.script: Teaching forces you to organize knowledge, identify gaps, and think from different angles. This is why 'learning by teaching' is so effective. Explaining to others clarifies your own understanding.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "To Teach Is to Learn"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Meeting the Learner
q2.script: Effective teaching starts where the learner is, not where the teacher is. What do they already know? What mental models do they have? Teaching builds bridges from existing understanding to new understanding.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Multiple Representations
q3.script: Different people understand differently—visual, verbal, through examples, through practice. Good teachers offer multiple paths to the same destination. If one explanation doesn't land, try another angle.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: To teach is to learn twice. Explaining to others reveals gaps in your own understanding. Want to master something? Teach it.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 218. Tomorrow, we'll explore density—how packed things are. Until then, try explaining something you're learning to someone else.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Teach to Learn - Explain Something
growTrack.activity: Take something you're learning or know well. Explain it to someone—a friend, family member, or even an imaginary student. Notice where you struggle to explain clearly. Those are your knowledge gaps. Teaching is learning.
